info.title: Ray API
info.description:
Multi-tenant notification delivery API. Authenticate with a tenant API key (`Authorization: Bearer ck_live_…`). All endpoints are tenant-scoped by the key.

Guides: https://ray.gege.mn/docs (every page also as markdown by appending `.md`; index for agents at https://ray.gege.mn/llms.txt).

Building with an AI coding agent? Install the [ray-skills](https://github.com/gege-mn/ray-skills) skill to integrate Ray automatically.

ApiKeyAuth.description: Tenant API key issued from the dashboard, e.g. `Authorization: Bearer ck_live_…`. Write endpoints require a key with the `write` scope.

JsonValue.description: Any JSON value: string, number, boolean, null, array, or nested object.

params.description: Template parameters for this delivery; falls back to the top-level `params` when omitted.

recipient.description: Channel-specific delivery target, validated against the channel of the chosen channelConfigId: `EmailRecipient` for ses_email and smtp_email, `FcmRecipient` for fcm_push, `TelegramRecipient` for telegram_bot, `TwilioSmsRecipient` for twilio_sms, `SendsmsMnRecipient` for sendsms_mn, and `{}` for slack_webhook, discord_webhook and generic_webhook (their destination is part of the channel config).

params.description: Template parameters substituted at render time. Values may be any JSON (strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, nested objects) so templates can iterate arrays/objects in `{{#section}}…{{/section}}` blocks. Scalars are escaped for the field they land in (see https://ray.gege.mn/docs/templates#escaping).

trackClicks.description: Email only. Rewrite body links through Ray for click tracking. Requires the server to have a click-tracking base URL configured.

campaignId.description: Free-form campaign id used to group click stats across sends.

priority.description: Dispatch priority. `high` (default) for transactional mail; set `low` for marketing/bulk so it never delays transactional sends sharing the same queue.

FcmRecipient.description: Per-send delivery target — supply exactly one of `deviceToken` or `topic`. Ray keeps no device registry: pass the FCM token (obtained from your client SDK and stored in your own system) on every send, or a topic name for multi-device fan-out. There is no "register device" step.

TwilioSmsRecipient.description: twilio_sms: an international number in E.164 form, e.g. +97699112233.

SendsmsMnRecipient.description: sendsms_mn: a Mongolian 8-digit number, e.g. 99112233 (+976 is stripped).

EmptyRecipient.description: slack_webhook, discord_webhook and generic_webhook take an empty recipient.

recipientSchema.description: Inline JSON Schema for the `recipient` object `POST /send` expects for this channel. The concrete shape varies by channel kind (e.g. `{ email }` for email, `{ deviceToken | topic }` for push).

channelConfigId.description: First delivery of the send; null for feed-only sends.

status.description: Always 'delivered' — feed entries exist independently of channel delivery state. Delivery diagnostics live on GET /sends/{id}.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page of `rows`; null when the page is the last one.

get.description: Prometheus text exposition. Gated by the `METRICS_AUTH_TOKEN` bearer when configured; otherwise open. Aggregates across every tenant.

get.summary: Resolve the current API key context

post.description: Renders content and enqueues delivery. Three modes: single-channel (top-level `channelConfigId` + `recipient` XOR `targets[]` fan-out), multi-channel (`deliveries[]` — the same logical notification over several channels for one recipient, each delivery with its own channel-shaped `recipient`; add `feed` for exactly one in-app feed entry), or feed-only (`feed` + `externalUserId` with no deliveries — a pure in-app notification). Per delivery, supply either `templateId` (+ `params`) to render a published template, or inline `content` (channel-shaped, with optional `params` + `logTitle`/`logDescription`) — exactly one of the two. Pass an `Idempotency-Key` header to make retries safe — replaying the same key with the same body returns the original result; a different body returns 409.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-generated key; result is cached for 24h.

409.description: Idempotency-Key reused with a different body

get.description: Discover the channels configured in your workspace, with the template kind each accepts and the JSON Schema for the `recipient` `POST /send` expects. Use the returned `id` as `channelConfigId`. Returns safe metadata only — never the channel's encrypted provider credentials.

post.summary: Send a test (is_test=true, never shown in customer feeds)

post.description: Restores an archived template. Names stay unique per tenant even while archived, so this is how a name held by an archived template is reclaimed (rather than recreating). Creating a template whose name collides with an archived one returns 409.

get.description: Cursor-paginated feed for one end user. `externalUserId` is required. Entries are created at send time (`feed` / `showInFeed`) and are independent of delivery state — they appear immediately (or at `notBefore` for scheduled sends) and are never hidden by a failed or suppressed delivery. `status` other than 'delivered' returns an empty page; test sends never create entries.
Status aggregate for the whole send plus one cursor-paginated page of its delivery rows (default 50, max 200), ordered `(createdAt, id)` ascending. Follow `nextCursor` for the rest.
Click counts grouped by destination URL for a send or campaign. Provide `sendId` or `campaignId` (at least one). Only links sent with `trackClicks: true` are counted.

Public, no API-key auth. Verifies the signed token, records the click, and 302-redirects to the destination URL carried in the token. A token is only honoured if its signature is valid, so this is not an open redirect.

post.summary: Create a webhook (returns the signing secret once)

patch.summary: Update a webhook (set rotateSecret to roll the signing key)

post.description: Model Context Protocol endpoint for AI agents and MCP clients (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, …). Stateless Streamable HTTP with JSON responses: send JSON-RPC 2.0 messages (`initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`) with `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`. Authenticate with the same API key as the REST API; a missing or malformed key is refused with 401 before any MCP processing, and `initialize` verifies the key. Each tool maps to one REST endpoint and is subject to the same scopes, rate limits and quota; REST failures come back as tool results with `isError: true`. JSON-RPC batches are not supported, and GET/DELETE return 405 (no SSE stream or sessions). Setup: https://ray.gege.mn/docs/ai-agents

schema.description: A single JSON-RPC 2.0 request or notification.

406.description: Accept header must include application/json and text/event-stream

post.description: Public, no API-key auth. The provider signature (SNS) is verified per request. URL embeds the channel config so a leaked URL can only target one config.

post.summary: Start a checkout for a paid plan (customer picks the provider)
post.description: Creates a Polar hosted checkout or a QPay invoice for the chosen plan. Returns the Polar `checkoutUrl`, or the QPay `invoiceId` + QR (`qrImage`/`qrText`/`shortUrl`). Returns 501 if the chosen provider or plan is not configured.
Public, no API-key auth. The Standard-Webhooks signature is verified against POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET before any state change; an invalid signature is rejected with 403.
Public, no API-key auth and no signature — the callback is an untrusted ping; Ray re-checks the invoice against QPay before granting access.
